verification_gap_identified: PSD-TELEMETRY-AUTH-001's own test (tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_telemetry_replay.py) only proves scripts/bootstrap.sh forwards a caller-supplied header through a stubbed urllib.request.urlopen; it never exercises the real /api/telemetry/replay Flask route or its @require_telemetry_authority(("operator","admin")) decorator in services/telemetry/auth.py. This task independently drives that real route with real JWTs.

finding.summary: Authorization: Bearer <trailing-whitespace-only> crashed validate_request_auth() with an unhandled IndexError, returning HTTP 500 instead of failing closed with 401 on the missing-authorization boundary.
finding.root_cause: token = raw.split(None, 1)[1].strip() if " " in raw else "" -- str.split(None, ...) strips trailing whitespace before splitting, so a header of exactly "Bearer " (or "Bearer" plus only whitespace) satisfies " " in raw but produces a single-element list, and [1] raises IndexError uncaught by the route's try/except TelemetryAuthorityError, surfacing as a raw Flask 500.
finding.fix: Replaced the split(None, 1) heuristic with a direct slice: token = raw[len("Bearer "):].strip(), which cannot raise IndexError and correctly falls through to the existing empty-token AuthError("401", ...) path for any whitespace-only remainder.
finding.blast_radius_note: services/runtime_auth_inbound.py is shared by telemetry, runtime-manager, control-plane/bff, capital, training-session, governance, and policy-learning auth call sites. Re-ran their existing auth-focused suites after the fix; all passed unchanged (see validation.regression_test_result).
